DEVELOPMENT PL AN REVIEW BO ARD
  MINUTES
  MARCH 9, 2023 at 8:30 AM
  245 EAST BONITA AVENUE
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS

  BOARD MEMBERS PRESENT

  Scott Dilley, Chamber of Commerce
  John Sorcinelli, Public Member at Large
  Margie Green, Planning Commission (Substitute for David Bratt)
  Brad McKinney, Assistant City Manager
  Shari Garwick, Director of Public Works
  Henry Noh, Director of Community Development

  BOARD MEMBERS ABSENT

  David Bratt, Planning Commission

  STAFF PRESENT

  Luis Torrico, Planning Manager
  Anne Nguyen, Associate Planner
  Victoria Gutierrez, Departmental Assistant

CALL TO ORDER

Scott Dilley called the regular meeting of the Developmental Plan Review Board to order at 8:34
a.m. so as to conduct regular business in the Council Chambers.

DPRB ITEMS

DPRB Case No. 22-0018
Associated Cases: ACCELA PROJ 22-0062

The Applicant, Peng Jiang, Jiang Architect Group, is requesting to construct a new 6,342
square-foot two-story single-family residence with a covered front porch and side porch totaling
920 square feet, and a 946 square-foot attached three-car garage on an existing 0.88-acre
vacant lot. The subject property is located at 325 Rebecca Drive (APN: 8382-018-083) within
Specific Plan No. 8.

Peng Jiang, Applicant was not present at the time.

Associate Planner Nguyen presented the staff report and recommended Board approval to the
Planning Commission.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked what materials would be used for the windows.
 DPRB Minutes  Page 2
March 9, 2023

Planning Manager Torrico stated the Applicant can clarity that.

Peng Jiang, Applicant arrived at 8:47 a.m.

Mr. Dilley asked if the front elevation is proposed with all stucco and no stone-work.

Associate Planner Nguyen answered that is correct.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked the Applicant if the proposed window materials are wood clad in aluminum
or vinyl and if the glass is reflective.

Peng Jiang, Applicant specified the proposed materials for the windows are clear-glazed, low-
heat glass with aluminum-clad wood frames. He added the materials have a good energy rating.
He stated he believed Associate Planner Nguyen gave a thorough presentation and he was
present to answer the Board’s questions.

Mrs. Green asked if this will be a speculative house or if they have a buyer.

Peng Jiang, Applicant said his client owns the property and the project is to build their dream
house, however the lot is currently vacant.

Mrs. Green asked why there seems to be two turn-arounds on the proposed driveway.

Community Development Director Noh stated the larger potion above the proposed turn-
around leads to 311 Rebecca Drive.

Peng Jiang, Applicant added that the proposed driveway will be patched to the existing driveway
for 311 Rebecca Drive at the property line and only one turn-around, in front of the proposed
garage, is part of the project. He stated this part of the project was very difficult but he spent a lot
of time working with the LA County Fire Department and received approval of the proposed plans.

Associate Planner Nguyen noted that the project received LA County Fire approval only
yesterday, March 22, 2023, and the Applicant provided stamped plans for Staff and the Board.

Planning Manager Torrico added that the owner of the adjacent property at 311 Rebecca Drive
spoke with Staff that morning about her concerns. He asked, on her behalf, if the entire existing
driveway will be replaced as part of the project.

Peng Jiang, Applicant stated they are proposing to replace only the portions of the existing
driveway that are within 325 Rebecca Drive, as it does not meet current LA County Fire standards,
and will patch to the driveway within 311 Rebecca Drive.

Planning Manager Torrico stated the existing driveway was built 20 years ago and the applicant
will need to verify that the new work will meet LA County Fire standards for concrete type and
thickness as well.

Peng Jiang, Applicant said the project plans have been reviewed and approved by LA County
Fire.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked if the pool will be built as part of the project.
 DPRB Minutes  Page 3
March 9, 2023

Peng Jiang, Applicant answered the pool will be included per the Client’s request and all
accessory structures that have been proposed to the Board are intended to be built as part of the
project.

There were no further comments to be heard.

Motion DPRB Case No. 22-0018

Mr. Sorcinelli moved to approve DPRB Case No. 22-0018 subject to the conditions of approval.

Motion seconded by Assistant City Manager McKinney.

Motion Carried: 6-0-0

OTHER BUSINESS

Report on Lighting Issue at 536 West Bonita Avenue

Planning Manager Torrico reported that at the February 9, 2023 DPRB Meeting, Mr. Sorcinelli
requested Staff to contact the owners of Sushiya restaurant located at 536 West Bonita Avenue
about their newly installed lighting. He stated that they installed two wall-pack light fixtures above
the front entrance and a third fixture under the covered walkway without permits and were in
violation of the San Dimas Municipal Code. Staff notified the owners of the restaurant and they
scheduled the removal of the two unpermitted light fixtures above the entrance for Saturday,
March 11, 2023. The third light fixture under the covered walkway could remain once permitted.
He stated that the business owners are working with Staff on installing appropriate, code-
compliant light fixtures.

Mr. Sorcinelli thanked Staff and stated the City should continue to monitor new lighting in
commercial areas and downtown.

Mrs. Green added that although the lights are very bright at Motel 6, she feels it is needed for
that area due to safety concerns.

Mr. Sorcinelli stated the City should try to maintain a standard City-wide. He suggested Staff
conduct a study to identify what current lighting issues to update and enforce standards. He
recommended the Board be involved in order to make recommendations.

Planning Manager Torrico stated Staff will discuss the matter and bring it back to the Board.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There were no comments to be heard.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business the meeting was adjourned at 9:15 a.m. to the meeting of March
23, 2023.
